**5B.6 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024**

**Bottom line:** *Mostly yes, but with important caveats.* The strongest 2024 evidence shows real investment in infrastructure/connectivity, administrative capacity, digital governance, and pro-investment regulation. The record is thinner on health-specific capital spending and large education-system buildout. Some economic measures were also visibly popularity-sensitive or still constrained by lingering digital controls.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `PBBM ushers Filipinos to a Bagong Pilipinas that serves its people` | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-02-15 | [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-ushers-filipinos-to-a-better-brighter-more-connected-bagong-pilipinas-with-the-philippine-domestic-submarine-cable-network-launch/) | Marcos launched domestic submarine-cable/connectivity expansion, improving backbone infrastructure for business, public services, and digital access. | `5B.6`; also `5B.4`, `5B.3` |
| `PBBM approves National Cybersecurity Plan to fortify PH against various threats` | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-02-08 | [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-approves-national-cybersecurity-plan-to-fortify-ph-against-various-threats/) | The administration adopted a cybersecurity plan with consultation from public, private, and academic stakeholders, which supports predictable digital governance. | `5B.6`; also `5B.4` |
| `PBBM adopts DICT's National Cybersecurity Plan 2023-2028` | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-06 | [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-adopts-dicts-national-cybersecurity-plan-2023-2028/) | EO 58 turned the cybersecurity plan into a whole-of-nation roadmap and required agencies/LGUs to implement and report, showing institutionalized admin capacity. | `5B.6`; also `5B.4` |
| `PBBM signs laws on streamlining procurement, combatting online scams` | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-07-20 | [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-signs-laws-on-streamlining-procurement-combatting-online-scams/) | Procurement reform standardized forms and institutionalized e-procurement, reducing favoritism, leakage, and transaction costs. | `5B.6`; also `5B.5`, `5B.4` |
| `The administration expanded eFOI access and kept a media-literacy / disinformation campaign in place` | Philippine News Agency | 2024-01-18 | [link](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1217036) | Expanded information access and anti-disinformation measures support administrative transparency and a more predictable operating environment. | `5B.6`; also `5B.4`, `5B.5` |
| `PBBM calls for comprehensive national flood-control plan to protect communities, production areas` | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-07-26 | [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-calls-for-comprehensive-national-flood-control-plan-to-protect-communities-production-areas/) | Marcos responded to severe flooding by calling for a national flood-control plan and expert-led policy updates, which is infrastructure/resilience investment. | `5B.6`; also `5B.3` |
| `PBBM SONA: AI, robotics, IoT, and cybersecurity training` | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-07-22 | [link](https://pco.gov.ph/presidential-speech/3rd-state-of-the-nation-address-of-his-excellency-ferdinand-r-marcos-jr-president-of-the-philippines-to-the-congress-of-the-philippines/) | He publicly pushed TVET and higher-education training in AI, robotics, IoT, and cybersecurity, which is a direct human-capital / technology-foundation signal. | `5B.6` |
| `Philippines signs tax reform law to lure foreign investment` | Reuters / Investing.com | 2024-11-10 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/philippines-marcos-signs-tax-reform-law-to-lure-foreign-investment-3713493) | CREATE MORE lowered corporate taxes and expanded incentives, improving the investment climate and job-creation rules, though at fiscal cost. | `5B.6`; also `5B.4`, `5B.3` |
| `FIRB increases IPA projects approval threshold to roll out red carpet to investors` | Department of Finance | 2024-02-19 | [link](https://www.dof.gov.ph/firb-increases-ipa-projects-approval-threshold-to-roll-out-red-carpet-to-investors/) | The economic team eased investment-approval rules, which directly improves the predictability of entry and approval for firms. | `5B.6`; also `5B.4` |
| `President Marcos unveils DA's Agri-Puhunan program` | Department of Agriculture | 2024-09-13 | [link](https://www.da.gov.ph/president-marcos-unveils-das-agri-puhunan-program-targeting-1-2-million-hectares-with-low-cost-credit-and-market-support/) | Low-cost credit, subsistence support, and market access for farmers are real productive-capacity measures, not just short-term relief. | `5B.6`; also `5B.3`, `5B.4` |
| `Internet freedom report, Philippines` | Freedom House | 2024 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-net/2024) | Freedom House said internet freedom declined, most Duterte-era site blocks remained, and brief network restrictions persisted, which weakens the case for fully open, predictable digital conditions. | `5B.6`; also `5B.4` |
| `Imports unlikely to cut rice prices` | BusinessWorld Online | 2024-07-09 | [link](https://www.bworldonline.com/the-nation/2024/07/09/607056/imports-unlikely-to-cut-rice-prices/) | Critics warned the rice-import strategy could favor importers and hurt farmers, suggesting some policy was politically driven and not purely rule-based productivity reform. | `5B.6`; also `5B.3`, `5B.4` |
| `Kilo rice still possible` | Reuters via Zawya | 2024-07-24 | [link](https://www.zawya.com/en/markets/commodities/0343-kilo-rice-still-possible-department-of-agriculture-philippines-vwstcm9g) | Reuters noted that cheap-rice targets were a campaign promise, which is evidence that some productivity policy was shaped by short-term popularity incentives. | `5B.6`; also `5B.3`, `5B.4` |
| `TeleRadyo Serbisyo joint venture / Prime Media Holdings` | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | [link](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines) | The report notes a media joint venture tied to Prime Media Holdings and the Romualdez family, an indirect sign that politically connected business networks still mattered under Marcos. | `5B.6`; also `5B.5` |

**Synthesis**
- Strongest pro-`5B.6` evidence: infrastructure/connectivity, cybersecurity governance, procurement reform, investment-rule easing, and agriculture productivity support.
- Weaker area: health. I did not find a comparably strong 2024 source showing major hospital/public-health capital expansion. Education evidence is real but mostly incremental, centered on TVET/AI upskilling rather than a large school-system buildout.
- Main negatives: lingering digital restrictions, some market interventions driven by campaign promises, and signs that politically connected business networks still operated in the environment.

**Search gap**
- Reliable 2024 evidence is sparse on direct health-system investment and on large, measurable education-capital programs. The available material is much stronger on infrastructure, digital capacity, and regulatory cleanup than on hospitals, clinics, teacher hiring, or school construction.
